concept: Rebuilding a time series collection with $out or mongorestore

claims.text: $out replaces an existing destination with the complete aggregation result. When timeseries options are supplied for an existing target, that target must be a time-series collection and its options must match. A rebuild that changes those options therefore needs a new destination. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-14)

The inspected mongorestore preflight rejects a native time-series restore when the destination already exists unless --drop is used, and rejects --noOptionsRestore for time-series intents. This guard applies to native time-series backups; it should not be confused with restoring regular staging BSON into a precreated time-series destination. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-30)

Extenify supplies its own Node.js migration example that converts daily snapshot dates to BSON dates, constructs item metadata, and writes listing_history with a timeseries $out. It advises running the migration before the daily writer starts because $out replaces the target. This is an authored implementation example, not an independent benchmark of fragmentation recovery. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-05)

For a rewrite with different time series options, use a new target name: $out requires the options to match when the destination already exists. A newly created target also needs the desired secondary indexes recreated; copying index definitions from an existing destination does not copy indexes from the source. (high confidence)

Order the measurement stream before rebuilding. The aggregation migration guide says $out does not guarantee output order and instructs users to sort before migration; the tools migration guide specifies oldest-to-newest insertion. --maintainInsertionOrder preserves dump order and cannot by itself turn an unordered dump into chronological data. (high confidence)

$out can read a sharded input but cannot write a sharded destination. Its comparison table also says $merge cannot write a time-series destination, so substituting $merge does not provide a time-series rebuild target. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-14)

Percona documents a restore failure for time-series collections with expireAfterSeconds: TTL deletion can remove buckets still needed by oplog replay, producing Location6781400, missing control field. Its PBM procedure disables ttlMonitorEnabled during restore and restores the original setting afterward. This evidence concerns PBM logical restore, not a demonstrated mongorestore workaround. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-30)

$out cannot write to a sharded output collection or run inside a transaction. $merge cannot output to a time series collection, so its append/merge semantics do not provide an alternative time series rebuild target. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-14)

For Percona Backup for MongoDB logical restore and PITR specifically, expireAfterSeconds can let the TTL monitor delete buckets needed by oplog replay, causing Location6781400: Time series bucket document is missing control field. Percona directs operators to save and disable ttlMonitorEnabled on every target data-bearing mongod for the restore, then restore each original value even on failure. This guidance is scoped to PBM, not established here for every mongorestore invocation. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-20)

For measurement-level rebuilding, MongoDB documents two routes: aggregate into a time-series destination with $out, or create the destination, dump a regular staging collection, and restore its BSON into that destination. Inference for fragmentation remediation: these routes submit measurements for fresh bucketing rather than merely copying an existing bucket dump. (medium confidence)

$out replaces an existing target rather than appending measurements. Its documented replacement procedure builds a temporary collection, copies existing index definitions, inserts results, and atomically replaces the target; failure leaves the pre-existing collection unchanged. An existing time series target must have exactly matching timeseries options. (low confidence)

A native time series mongodump/mongorestore round trip is not evidence of measurement rebucketing. The tools implementation dumps bucket data and recognizes system.buckets BSON as a time series restore intent. Inference: to remediate sparse buckets by reinsertion, first materialize logical measurements rather than assuming a native backup restore merges their buckets. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-30)

The precise documented minimum for $out to a time series target is MongoDB 7.0.3 on the 7.0 branch, or 7.1; the migration overview says 7.0 less precisely. The output must specify timeseries with a timeField; metaField and granularity can be supplied. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-14)

MongoDB documents $out replacement as temporary-collection creation, index-definition copying, document insertion, and an atomic replacement on completion. If the aggregation fails, the previous destination remains unchanged; this does not by itself define an application write-catch-up procedure. (low confidence)

In the regular-collection-to-time-series tools workflow, MongoDB specifies --noIndexRestore and manual recreation of secondary indexes. This is a measurement migration recipe, distinct from the separate documented example that backs up and restores an existing time-series collection with namespace remapping. (medium confidence)

The inspected mongodump implementation explicitly says that specifying a time-series collection dumps its system.buckets collection. For the legacy bucket namespace path, a native time-series dump is therefore a bucket backup. Inference: a native dump/restore should not be presented as a demonstrated measurement rebucketing or sparse-bucket consolidation operation. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-30)

A first-hand Stack Overflow question dated May 14, 2022 reports that restoring a dump into an existing time-series collection requires --drop and would remove existing data. The retrieved thread provides no accepted solution. Treat it as historical operational evidence, not a current patch-version support matrix. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-31)

Rebuilding through an aggregation reads logical measurements and writes them to a new time series target using a final $out stage with timeseries options. This is a measurement rewrite; the cited migration procedures do not promise a particular reduction in bucket count or disk usage. (high confidence)

The documented tools migration path precreates a time series destination, optionally materializes transformed measurements in an ordinary staging collection, dumps that non-time-series collection, and restores its BSON into the destination with --noIndexRestore and --maintainInsertionOrder, without dropping the destination. The guide instructs users to recreate secondary indexes afterward. (low confidence)

Native time series restore can encounter an existing destination bucket collection: mongorestore preflight rejects that condition and requests removal. Do not conflate native time series backup restore with restoring ordinary measurement BSON into a precreated time series collection. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-30)
